summary: @onereach/lambda-invocation ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing 727KB obfuscated Bun payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v...`), extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. Bun is downloaded and used to run the bundled file even when Bun is already present on the host, so the alternate runtime is unconditionally used to execute the shipped payload. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle (sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc) obfuscated with string-array rotation (`WV8StW` rotating array `n7gIxM`), codepoint-based string reconstruction (`hc1jfK9`), and hex-mangled identifiers, making its behavior opaque to static inspection. The package advertises itself as a thin AWS Lambda invocation helper; shipping and executing an opaque 727KB Bun-only bundle named `math_init.js` from a preinstall hook is inconsistent with that stated purpose. `npm install` auto-executes `preinstall` on every consumer, so installing this version causes the obfuscated payload to run under the freshly downloaded Bun runtime on developer and CI hosts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
